title: Moho animated value ("channel")
description: Almost every numeric/colour/boolean/string property in a Moho document is stored as this one repeated structure - confirmed 201,185+ instances across the reverse-engineering sample set (see docs/moho-project-file-format.md §5). A field that is never animated may instead appear as a bare scalar or plain object (see ChannelOrPlain below) - Moho accepts both forms transparently.

InterpEntry.description: One entry of a channel's interp[] array, one per keyframe, describing the interpolation of the segment LEAVING that keyframe. moho2svg.py ignores this entirely and always interpolates linearly - exact at keyframes, approximate between them. The meaning of t/im/in/s/h is NOT decoded; only the observed value sets are recorded here. See docs/moho-project-file-format.md §5.3.

t.description: NOT the interpolation type - that is `im`. Observed 0 on 2,662,751 of 2,664,273 entries (76-document corpus scan; the 1,873,377 count above was a 46-document artefact), with 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 256, 259 and 260 in the remainder, almost exclusively on pose/anim_pos/anim_angle/anim_scale/physics_motor_speed. Most likely the keyframe's LABEL COLOUR (manual ch. 16.13 lists a Label among a keyframe's settings and offers eleven colours); still not confirmed. An earlier revision of this schema called this the interpolation type, which is what sent moho2svg.py looking for the easing enum in the wrong field. M1.5 batch 7: CLAUDE.md's `pkg_moho.lua_pkg` struct-order decode names this field (`tags`) but moho2svg.py's Channel/_segment/_smooth/_parse_cycles never read it (grepped directly - only `im`/`v1`/`v2` are consumed), so MODELLED does not apply; probed instead. Forced to 999 (a value never seen in the corpus) on every one of Bandit.mohoproj's 10,074 interp entries at frame 28 (between two real keyframes of a bone whose own interp entries carry non-zero `t`): inert.
t.x-moho-evidence: docs/moho-field-probes.md: t=999, 10074 sites, Bandit.mohoproj frame 28, inert. Not read by moho2svg.py (Channel.of/_segment/_smooth/_parse_cycles only consume im/v1/v2).

im.description: The INTERPOLATION METHOD for the segment leaving this keyframe (manual ch. 16.06 names the methods; ch. 16.13's keyframe dialog is what maps them onto this entry's fields). An ENUM, not a bitfield. Decoded by rendering a controlled two-keyframe motion with Moho's own CLI at each value and reading the curve back: 0 = Linear (exact), 1 = Smooth (exact; Moho's default and 88.4% of all keyframes), 3 = Step (exact), 5 = Cycle, 6 = also exactly linear, 9 = Bezier (confirmed by a 1:1 match with the `b` block - 238 of 238 entries carrying one have im=9). 2, 4, 7, 8, 10 and 11 have measured curves that are not yet reproduced. Corpus distribution: 1 (1,656,205), 3 (151,483), 0 (54,456), 5 (3,136), 11 (2,916), 2 (2,582), 6 (1,495), 10 (798), 9 (238), 8 (34), 7 (27), 4 (7).
im.x-moho-evidence: moho2svg.py Channel._segment dispatches Linear/Smooth/Step/Pose exactly, the other 7 values fall back to an inferred cubic; measured against Moho's own rendered curves, see docs/moho-project-file-format.md §5.3

in.description: The keyframe's ANIMATION INTERVAL (manual ch. 16.07: interpolation is recomputed only every n-th frame, n between 1 and 6). Observed 1 (2,629,519 of 2,664,273 entries, 76-document scan), 0 (32,764), 3 (1,348), 2 (634), 8 (8). M1.5 batch 7: CLAUDE.md's struct-order decode names this field but moho2svg.py never reads it (only im/v1/v2 are consumed - grepped directly), so EDITABLE is the right disposition, not MODELLED. NEWLY CONFIRMED, not merely 'almost certainly': forced to 6 (a value never seen in the corpus, still inside the manual's documented 1-6 range) on every one of Bandit.mohoproj's 10,074 interp entries at frame 28 (between two real keyframes): **AFFECTS RENDER** - visually confirmed by rendering both twins and viewing the PNGs (a real, plausible pose shift on Bandit's hat/torso silhouette, not a glitch), the first direct confirmation this field does anything in Moho's own renderer.

v1.description: A general-purpose slot whose meaning depends on `im`. For im=5 (Cycle) it is the RELATIVE cycle length in frames when >= 0. Otherwise it holds the untouched default 0.1, or a -1 / -1000000 sentinel. See Channel._parse_cycles.
v1.x-moho-evidence: moho2svg.py:1958 in Channel._parse_cycles (trace: out/traced_keys.json, see tools/trace_fields.py)

v2.description: The second general-purpose slot. For im=5 (Cycle) it is the ABSOLUTE frame to resume at, used when v1 < 0. Otherwise the default 0.5, or a -1 / -1000000 sentinel. See Channel._parse_cycles.

b.description: Explicit Bezier handles for the timing curve itself, one object per control point. Present on exactly 238 entries, and EVERY one of them has im == 9 - which is what identifies im=9 as Bezier interpolation. Not read by moho2svg.py, so an im=9 keyframe falls back to the generic curve. (An earlier revision said these appear only alongside t==4; the correlation is with `im`, not `t`.) NOTE: an earlier seeding pass mis-annotated this MODELLED, citing Color.from_raw as evidence - that function reads an UNRELATED field, ColorValue's own `b` (the blue channel), which merely shares this name; the flat-by-name registry borrowed its true claim for this one. Caught by check_field_coverage.py's rule 4 (a MODELLED key whose own description asserts no read at all) - see docs/moho-field-coverage-plan.md Task 8 fix round 1. FOLLOW-UP: correcting this field's OWN disposition back to UNKNOWN left it declared FIRST in this file, still shadowing ColorValue.b/PlainRGBA.b (both genuinely MODELLED) under load_registry's first-occurrence-wins - the flat corpus key `b` flipped from a false MODELLED claim to a false UNCOVERED one. Fixed generally, not by reordering this pair: check_field_coverage.py's rule 5 (find_disposition_conflicts) now fails on any such cross-occurrence disagreement unless waived, and effective_disposition() scores a flat key as covered when ANY of its occurrences is MODELLED/EDITABLE - see ColorValue.b's own x-moho-registry-conflict-waived and docs/moho-field-coverage-plan.md Task 8 fix round 4.

ao.description: Presumably the OUTGOING Bezier timing-handle angle/magnitude at this control point (paired with `ai` for the incoming side). M1.5 batch 7: not read by moho2svg.py under any name (this `b` array itself is confirmed unread - see the array's own entry above), so EDITABLE not MODELLED. Probed on a real im=9 (Bezier) entry: Bandit.mohoproj's bones 3/4/5 `anim_angle` channels carry 16 such entries corpus-wide within this one document. Forced to -5.0 (well outside the corpus range [-1.553343, 0.547067]) at frame 28 (inside bone 3's own [25,33] Bezier segment): **AFFECTS RENDER** - a real, reproducible pixel difference (23 pixels, a thin 2-pixel sliver at the canvas's left edge), independently reproduced during review. **This is weaker evidence than it may look, and weaker than h/in's own finding below - flagged explicitly rather than left implied.** A follow-up sweep (review) of neighbouring values (-1, -2, -3, -8, -10, -15, +5, +10) all came back INERT, and only a much larger +20 (not the -5.0 tried here) triggered a difference elsewhere - a non-monotonic, narrow pattern more consistent with a coincidental threshold/clip-boundary crossing at this one specific value than with a systematic interpolation-shape effect. Whether `ao` genuinely shapes the Bezier timing curve, or the -5.0 fixture happened to cross some unrelated clip/rounding boundary, is NOT established by this probe. This does not change the disposition (EDITABLE - unread by moho2svg.py, a real measured difference exists) but does mean the evidence should not be read as comparable in kind to `h`/`in` (robust, large, spanning a real silhouette region at every value tried).
ao.x-moho-evidence: docs/moho-field-probes.md: ao=-5.0, 16 sites, Bandit.mohoproj frame 28, AFFECTS RENDER (23 differing pixels, independently reproduced; nearby values -1/-2/-3/-8/-10/-15/+5/+10 all inert - narrow, non-monotonic, possibly a threshold/clip-boundary crossing rather than a systematic effect). Not read by moho2svg.py.

ActionRef.description: One entry of a channel's actions[] list: this channel takes its value from `pose` instead of its own when/val while the Smart Bone dial named `name` is active. `pose` is itself a full channel of the SAME type as the parent channel, but keyed by "pose-curve position" rather than by document frame - see docs/moho-project-file-format.md §11 and §5.4 for how the active pose-frame is found (inverting the pose curve against the dial's own current angle).

name.description: An action name, matched against a registry on some ancestor BoneLayer's own `actions` list. If this name also matches a bone's own name in the same skeleton, that bone is the "dial" whose angle drives this override; otherwise this pose is dormant (this tool only activates the dial kind).

_ChannelBase.description: Fields common to every channel regardless of `type`. `when`, `val`, and `interp` are always exactly the same length (verified with zero exceptions across the entire sample set).

ref.description: Marks a channel whose keyframes come from an action inserted BY REFERENCE rather than by copy - manual ch. 17.02: "Moho will insert a special keyframe in the Mainline that refers back to the action you used ... changes will automatically be reflected in the mainline", as against Insert Copy, which just copies the keyframes in. NOT read by either exporter. **Corrected (M1.5 batch 7):** an earlier revision of this description said "true on 1,431 channels in 5 documents" (a 46-document sample); a fresh 76-document scan finds it true in 24 documents, not 5 - the stale count is superseded, not merely re-confirmed. M1.5 batch 7 also closes the "whether ignoring it changes any rendered pixel" gap: forced true on EVERY channel in Bandit.mohoproj (7,898 sites, most of them a real false->true change - Bandit is itself one of the 24 true-somewhere documents) at frame 25: inert, a maximally strong negative (every channel in the document, not a sample).
ref.x-moho-evidence: docs/moho-field-probes.md: ref=true, 7898 sites (document-wide, every channel), Bandit.mohoproj frame 25, inert. Not read by moho2svg.py/moho2lottie.py.

split.description: Vec2/Vec3 channels only, and rare. **Corrected (M1.5 batch 7):** an earlier revision of this description said "observed exactly once" (a 46-document sample); a fresh 76-document scan finds it on exactly 3 documents (Bandit.mohoproj, Scene 5.moho, Whale.mohoproj - 1 site each). One independent Val sub-channel per axis (Moho's "separate the x/y curves" feature). moho2svg.py does not read this - it evaluates the parent Vec2/Vec3 arrays directly, which could go stale if an axis is keyframed differently from its parent. **THIS IS NOW CONFIRMED TO MATTER TO MOHO ITSELF, not merely a theoretical staleness risk**: probed on Bandit.mohoproj's own real site (bone 12's `anim_pos`, split into independent x/y Val sub-channels), forcing both sub-channels' `val` to 5.0 (wildly different from the parent Vec2's own keyframed x/y) at frame 30 (inside the sub-channel's own animated span): **AFFECTS RENDER**. So Moho's own renderer DOES honour the split sub-channels (at least here), and a document whose split axis is keyframed differently from its parent - the exact staleness scenario this description already warned about - would render differently in Moho than in this exporter's fixed-camera, parent-array-only model. See docs/moho-project-file-format.md §5.4. **NOT simple linear substitution - review found the effect is non-monotonic at the extreme**: `val=-50.0` came back INERT on two separate runs, while the `+5.0` tried here and a further `+50.0` both AFFECT RENDER. Whoever next touches this field should not assume a monotonic value->pixel relationship from the one forced value this probe used.
split.x-moho-evidence: docs/moho-field-probes.md: split=[{Val 5.0},{Val 5.0}], 1 site, Bandit.mohoproj frame 30, AFFECTS RENDER (329,585 differing pixels, a large real silhouette change - robust at this value; review found val=-50.0 comes back inert on two runs while +5.0/+50.0 both affect render, i.e. non-monotonic, not simple substitution). Not read by moho2svg.py/moho2lottie.py (a real gap, not merely an unread-but-harmless field).

StringChannel.description: A string channel. Used for switch_keys (child layer names), shape_order, layer_ordering, timeline_markers.

Channel.description: A channel of any of the six observed types. Prefer the specific *Channel $defs (ValChannel, ColorChannel, ...) wherever the expected type is known from context - this generic union exists for places (e.g. an action's pose, a split axis) where the type must match whatever the sibling/parent channel already uses.
